scope: Constitutive inversion, observation, reconstruction, conditional energy identities, global existence and uniqueness for globally Lipschitz Hilbert fields, and actual finite-matrix split iteration with O(1/n) convergence. This is not a continuum limit, a dimension-uniform bound, or a closed solution of general periodic nonlinear PDEs. Additionally, the original inviscid periodic Kerr PDE is constructed for the fixed analytic initial class (weighted branch norm at most 57/250 and 0 <= T <= 1/5), with actual initial attainment, cutoff-independent analytic tail controls, and a joint Fourier/time-iteration limit, including a certified mixed-wave input. This does not assert a general large-data or postshock inviscid continuum limit.
adaptation: Imported module bodies and namespaces are unchanged: only complete import lines are removed. Repository-native bridges are separately authored proofs, identified by native_bridges; they are not import-only adaptations. The joint assembly context listed in assembly_contexts adds two namespace-qualified Set aliases outside the exact HilbertFlow source byte span.

native_bridges.authorship_description: New proof body authored in primitive-lean: instantiate the abstract Hilbert results with an arbitrary finite real matrix and the existing scalar materialInverse; identify the existing ExactShear iteration and recover physical electric and magnetic fields.

New input-only continuum certificate authored in primitive-lean: bundle the actual analytic Maxwell fields, initial attainment, spatial Galerkin error, explicit splitting diagonal and uniform joint limit; specialize to the committed sinusoidal input.

assembly_contexts.reason: Earlier joint supplements open Finset outside their namespaces. Add namespace-qualified aliases of Set.piecewise and Set.union_comm before the exact HilbertFlow source so its original unqualified rewrite names retain their standalone meanings. These export aliases may persist after the surrounding section; no source bytes or proof declarations are changed.
